Author: Hao Toan
Message:
refactor(config): every environment variable is a named, typed field of config; no company domains in code

config.ts is the only reader of process.env for configuration. Each variable is mapped once, when it loads, to a named
field (config.server.host, config.hasakiWorkBrowser.chromeProfile, config.agent.cursorTimeoutMs, config.auth.secret, ...);
call sites use those fields. Company endpoints (Argo CD, Vault, Kafka, Splunk, Hasaki Work, file base URL, Bitbucket
workspace, production domains) default to empty and come from .env (new keys documented in .env.example); tests set
placeholder example domains in test/env.ts.

- Booleans accept 1/true/yes/on and 0/false/no/off for every flag (CODEACT_ENABLED and LSP_ENABLED previously took only "1").
- PORT and ANALYTICS_TIMEOUT_MS must be integers (the server refuses to start otherwise); CURSOR_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS falls
  back to 45 minutes with a warning. One parse for what two call sites parsed differently.
- RETRIEVAL_INTERNAL_TOKEN is config.retrieval.internalToken (generated token no longer written into process.env);
  platform-go gets DATABASE_URL and the token explicitly.
- config.agent.claudeBin / cursorBin hold the resolved executable (env > config.json > bundled), replacing eight repeated
  "CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE || config.agent.claudeBin" expressions.
- Child processes of the git, platform-go and open-code-review launchers no longer inherit AUTH_SECRET, DATABASE_URL,
  the internal token or the git tokens (src/platform/childEnv.ts).
- eslint.config.mjs forbids process.env under src/ outside an explicit, commented allowlist (standalone children and
  launchers); README no longer says config.json is unread.
- Tests that change these settings at run time now set the config field (and process.env where a child must see it).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Author: Hao Toan
Message:
fix(codeact): end-to-end cancellation and exact terminal persistence

- The workflow surface passes the attempt's execution signal (run
  cancellation, lease loss, attempt timeout) to executeCode, as Chat
  already did; nested calls carry their own signal into callTool.
- callTool accepts ToolCallContext.signal: it never starts a handler
  after the abort and never reports a result that arrived after it
  (handlers may forward the signal to their I/O; none does yet).
- code_executions: the terminal transition only updates a running row;
  rows left running by a dead worker are reconciled as interrupted
  before each execution (partial index, migration 091).
- Answers for oversized results carry original_bytes and a note on how
  to narrow the query.
- Tests: attempt cancellation mid nested call, expired lease, registry
  abort semantics, single terminal status, structured overflow with
  redaction; real-sandbox cancellation and IPC flood leave no process.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Hao Toan
Message:
feat(security): runtime provenance at chat operation sinks

Before a mutating operation is proposed, each declared sink field
(kafka.publish cluster/topic and payload; qc_http.request url and
payload) is traced to the platform's own records of the conversation:
the owner's words or the operator's pre-authorized scope (trusted), a
tool result / CodeAct output / document (untrusted), or nowhere
(unknown). An untrusted target is refused; an unknown target or an
observed payload must be confirmed by the owner and never takes the
pre-authorized auto path. Decisions are stored on the operation
(migration 090) and audited with record refs, never values. A unit
test requires every mutating registry tool to declare its sink fields.
ADR 0010 documents coverage and the uninstrumented native-tool path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Description: Identified a Private Key, which may compromise cryptographic security and sensitive data encryption.
Author: Bành Hảo Toàn
Message:
feat(git): add GitLab SSH transport and MR review comments

Review found two required capabilities missing from the GitLab change:
SSH authentication for Git operations, and a caller for posting review
comments on merge requests.

- SSH: per-user key (user secret gitlab_ssh_key:<host>) plus host keys
  pinned per instance (config.gitlab.instances[].sshHostKeys, sshPort).
  remoteGit writes the key and a known_hosts with only the pinned keys as
  0600 files in its temp dir, runs ssh with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes and
  BatchMode, allows only protocol.ssh, and rewrites the canonical HTTPS URL
  with a command-line insteadOf so Git config keeps the HTTPS identity.
  Without both pieces the HTTPS token transport is used as before.
- Review comments: the PR step posts the run's review findings as one MR
  comment through provider.commentOnPullRequest, with a per-run marker so
  retries skip it; secrets are masked and failures never fail the PR.
- Smaller gaps: git.repository tool (default and protected branches),
  GitLab tokens masked in trace values, refused merge/close actions are
  audited.

Author: Bành Hảo Toàn
Message:
feat(eval): unblock live provider evaluation with hard budgets

Live evaluation was blocked outright because nothing enforced token/cost caps
or isolation, so provider and context changes could not be measured. Live
phases now reuse the production agent executor in isolated eval worktrees with
a throwaway database and provider sandboxes. They abort on case token, cost or
wall-clock budgets and a shared suite cost cap. Live runs still need admin paid
approval and are blocked with a reason when a prerequisite is missing. Also
arm provider abort listeners when the signal fired during preparation.
